rationale:
Evidence. Iteration 5 (score 382.3) is the best design so far. Its oval finished 19 of 20 runs at 1.95 s, but the s-bend (progress 0.44) and slalom (progress 0.12, 1.4 line-loss events per run) still left the tape. Iteration 6 widened the sensor array to ±0.06 m and raised ki to its 5.0 limit. Its score fell to 269.5: oval finish rate dropped from 0.95 to 0.40 and oval max_error rose, while the s-bend gained only a little (progress 0.48). The wider array therefore did not help, and it probably coarsened the edge readings. Steering oscillation is 0.13 to 0.33 and max_error sits at the 0.06 m off-track limit on every track. The robot is not jittering badly, but it overshoots into bends and then drifts out.

Decision. I revert the geometry to the iteration 5 layout (five sensors at x = -0.04 to +0.04 in 0.02 m steps, y = 0.06, 16 mm footprint). I keep ki at 4.0, the value that gave the best score, rather than the 5.0 that hurt the oval. The one controller change is kd from 0.9 to 1.2, to damp the transient overshoot into bends, which is the mechanism most consistent with max_error reaching the limit with low RMS. kp (5.0), base_speed (1.2) and line_loss (last_direction) are unchanged, so the effect of kd can be read against iteration 5.

Expected result. Oval finish rate should hold near 0.95 with completion time about 2 s. The s-bend and slalom should show higher progress and fewer off-track endings. Score should rise above 382 if the overshoot hypothesis is right.

Hypotheses. H1: the s-bend and slalom failures are transient overshoot, so higher kd raises their progress. H2: if kd alone does not help and the s-bend still ends off track with low RMS, turn-in speed is the limit and base_speed should drop to about 1.1. H3: slalom line loss is caused by fast direction changes at the 0.04 m array edge, so the next test should try a 7-sensor array at ±0.045 m, not a wider 5-sensor one.

Measurements requested: completion, progress, completion_time, rms_error, max_error, line_loss_events, steering_oscillation, control_effort, controller_errors and noise_robustness, reported per track, so that overshoot, edge loss and speed effects can be separated.
